**Answer:** the responsive styling lives in a set of plain CSS files under `sanic/pages/styles/`, wired into the page classes by a small metaclass — with the actual viewport/mobile logic concentrated in **`sanic/pages/styles/BasePage.css`** (shared by both page types), plus page-specific sheets `ErrorPage.css` and `DirectoryPage.css`.

### How the responsive part actually works

There is no media-query-per-breakpoint framework and no external stylesheet request — it's one breakpoint plus fluid root font sizing:

- **One breakpoint, `@media (max-width: 1000px)`** in `BasePage.css`. Inside it, two things change:
  - `body > *` padding tightens from `1rem 2vw` to `0.5rem 1.5vw`;
  - `html` gets `font-size: calc(6px + 10 * 100vw / 1000);` — the comment in the file calls it "Scale everything by rem of 6px-16px by viewport width". So the root `rem` slides from 16px down to 6px as the viewport narrows, and **every size in the sheets is expressed in `rem`** (`body`, `h1`–`h3`, `.smalltext`, the tables) precisely so it all scales with the viewport instead of overflowing on a phone.
- **`vw`-based horizontal padding** (`2vw` / `1.5vw`) in the default rules, so gutters are already proportional before the breakpoint kicks in.
- **Width clamping** on the shared `.container` class (`min-width: 600px` / `max-width: 1600px`), which `DirectoryPage` applies as `table(class_="autoinindex container")`.
- **`@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`** re-declares the `:root` custom properties for dark mode — the other viewport/environment-dependent styling in the same base sheet.

### How the sheets get to the page

`sanic/pages/css.py`:

- `_extract_style(view_query, name)` — if a class declares `STYLE_FILE`, that value is read as a file when the path exists, otherwise used as literal CSS; with no `STYLE_FILE`, it reads `sanic/pages/styles/<ClassName>.css` (`CURRENT_DIR = Path(__file__).parent`), returning `""` if absent.
- `class CSS(ABCMeta).__new__` sets `Page.STYLE` (plus any `STYLE_APPEND`), then builds `Page.CSS = "".join(Class.STYLE for Class in reversed(Page.__mro__) if type(Class) is CSS)` — i.e. it cascades ancestor sheets, so `BasePage.css` always precedes the subclass sheet and page-specific rules win.
- `BasePage._head()` renders it inline: `self.doc.style(HTML(self.style))`, so the responsive CSS ships inside every generated error page / directory listing.

`ErrorPage` adds one twist: `STYLE_APPEND = tracerite.html.style` appends tracerite's traceback CSS, and its traceback is rendered with `include_js_css=False` to avoid duplicating it.

**Answer:** `sanic/pages/styles/BasePage.css` — the stylesheet attached to `BasePage` in `sanic/pages/base.py`.

How it's wired (at commit `57d44f2`):

- **`sanic/pages/css.py`** — a `CSS(ABCMeta)` metaclass. In `__new__` it calls `_extract_style(...)`, which loads `sanic/pages/styles/f"{name}.css"` (or a `STYLE_FILE` override / literal `STYLE` string) and then builds `Page.CSS` by concatenating the `STYLE` of every ancestor in `reversed(Page.__mro__)` whose metaclass is `CSS`. So subclasses inherit their parent's rules automatically.
- **`sanic/pages/base.py`** — `class BasePage(ABC, metaclass=CSS)`; `BasePage.STYLE` becomes the contents of `styles/BasePage.css`, exposed via the `style` property. `BasePage._head()` injects it inline: `self.doc.style(HTML(self.style))`.
- **`sanic/pages/error.py`** (error pages) and **`sanic/pages/directory_page.py`** (directory listings) both subclass `BasePage`, so the responsive rules come from `BasePage.css`; each can only append its own via `STYLE` / `STYLE_APPEND` (their files are `ErrorPage.css` and `DirectoryPage.css`).

The viewport-dependent / mobile parts live in those two files — a code search over `sanic/pages` for `@media` matches only `styles/BasePage.css` and `styles/DirectoryPage.css`:

- `BasePage.css` uses a viewport-relative root font size, `html { font-size: calc(... 100vw ...) }`, so all `rem`-based sizing scales with viewport width; a `@media (max-width: 1000px)` block re-adjusts that font size and shrinks box padding on `body > *` for narrow screens; `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` swaps the `--background-color`-style custom properties for dark mode.
- `DirectoryPage.css` adds its own width-based queries for the listing table/grid (column hiding and wrapping at small widths).

So: framework = plain inline CSS built by the `CSS` metaclass, not an external library; responsive behaviour = `sanic/pages/styles/BasePage.css` (shared), extended per page in `styles/DirectoryPage.css` and `styles/ErrorPage.css`.
